newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth seeks to set up own CLEC unit.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth seeks to set up own CLEC unit.

text.p: BellSouth Corp said Tuesday it is creating a new unit to operate as a competitive local exchange carrier in a move to penetrate local phone markets outside its immediate franchise area.

Pending regulatory approval, the Baby Bell operator said the new unit will set up operations both inside and outside BellSouth's nine-state operating region. It intends to have the unit offer the same range of services as BellSouth, it said.
BellSouth plans to have the new unit -- headquartered in Atlanta -- fully operational by mid-1998, it said.
The move "will allow the company to meet new telecommunications competitors on equal footing," particularly in the realm of pricing adjustments, it said in a press release.
Currently it must seek regulatory approval for all price adjustments, but as a CLEC, the new unit will be able to "react to market conditions just as our competitors do."

"Furthermore, the new subsidiary would allow us to extend service to select markets throughout the southern United States that we don't currently serve, and give us the ability to follow our customers to markets outside the Southern United States where those customers need integrated communications service," BellSouth marketing vice president Richard Anderson said.
